story.title: The Ghost Frequency
story.logline: A lonely audio archivist discovers her dead brother's voice hidden in white noise, only to realize the broadcast is coming from inside her own throat.
story.theme: Grief alters our perception of reality until we become the ghosts we chase.
story.twist: The audio signals are not coming from the vintage radio, but are actually vibrations originating from her own vocal cords.
story.ending: If I am the one speaking the past into the dark, then who is listening to me right now?

scenes.narration: My dead brother just spoke to me through a broken radio.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close up of Maya, 25, short black hair, wearing an oversized grey hoodie, sitting in a dimly lit, cluttered attic full of old analog tape machines and glowing vacuum tubes.
scenes.camera: Extreme close up on Maya's eyes widening, rapid push-in.

scenes.narration: Leo died three years ago in a car crash. Yet his exact voice crackles from this dusty speaker right now.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, staring intensely at a glowing vintage Zenith radio on a wooden desk covered in magnetic tape.

scenes.narration: I press record. I need to capture the proof. The static shrieks back, burying his whispered warning underneath rising electronic noise.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, trembling hands slamming down the red record button on a heavy reel-to-reel deck.
scenes.camera: Low angle looking up at Maya's frantic expression.

scenes.narration: He says my name. He tells me to stop listening to the ghosts before the feedback loop consumes my entire mind.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, pressing both hands against her ears while neon waveforms spike wildly on a computer monitor.
scenes.camera: Handheld jittery camera shaking with the audio distortion.

scenes.narration: I unplug the radio. Total silence fills the attic. But the voice doesn't stop. It echoes louder inside my skull.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, backing away from the dead radio into the shadowy corner of the dusty attic.
scenes.camera: Wide shot pulling backward away from Maya.

scenes.narration: I touch my throat. It vibrates like a guitar string, humming with the exact radio frequency that Leo used.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, trembling fingers pressing directly against her own larynx in the dark room.
scenes.camera: Tight macro shot on her fingers touching her throat.

scenes.narration: The waveform on my screen proves the truth. The audio isn't broadcasting into the room. It is coming straight from me.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, staring in absolute horror at a laptop screen showing audio waves matching her throat movements.
scenes.camera: Over the shoulder shot framing the glowing screen.

scenes.narration: I am the transmitter. Every tear, every desperate midnight wish I whispered to his memory built this impossible machine.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, sitting frozen as ghostly blue light emanates from her skin in the dark attic.
scenes.camera: Static medium shot centering her symmetrical face.

scenes.narration: Leo never spoke to me. I simply learned how to mimic his ghost so I wouldn't have to face the quiet.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, closing her eyes as her mouth moves without any external sound escaping her lips.
scenes.camera: Slow push-in on her closed lips.

scenes.narration: If I am the one speaking the past into the dark, then who is listening to me right now?
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, short black hair, oversized grey hoodie, staring directly into the camera lens as the screen glitches into heavy white noise.
scenes.camera: Extreme close up locking eyes directly with the viewer.

caption.hook: I found my dead brother in the static.
caption.title: The Ghost Frequency
caption.caption:
Hours spent isolating lost audio finally brought him back, but the vintage radio wasn't receiving a signal. The vibrations were coming from inside me.

Are we ever truly alone, or are we just haunting ourselves?
